pr.title: test: align read privacy and secret fixtures
pr.body:
The verifier-failure fixture expected a detailed protected-query log that the current read privacy policy intentionally suppresses. Assert the bounded process denial and absence of query diagnostics separately while retaining both 503 responses, two verifier attempts with their exact identities, empty response bodies, and zero domain execution.

Use fresh nonfunctional privacy/invocation canaries and unambiguous initializers so the unchanged reusable-secret scanner evaluates the fixtures correctly. Production security, privacy, scanner rules, workflows, native cases, budgets, tools, and source pins are unchanged.

Validation: the two original failures were reproduced; 124 focused test executions passed (86 trust-boundary, 16 privacy, 17 invocation, 5 strict secret controls), with no failures or skips. Three Release/package builds passed with no warnings or errors. Full current-source CI and native integration remain required.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Test-only fixture and assertion updates; production security, privacy middleware, and scanner rules are unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> Updates **test expectations and fixtures only** so they match current read-privacy behavior and reusable-secret scanning—no production or policy changes.
> 
> **Administrator verifier failure (Story 5.5 P-4):** `WireAdministratorFlag_VerifierFailure_FailsClosedWithBoundedUnavailable` no longer expects a second bounded denial log on protected `/query`. It now asserts a single process-path denial (`Path=/process`, 503, correlation id), **unchanged log output after the query** (detailed read diagnostics suppressed), empty 503 bodies, and **two verifier invocations** with the expected tenant/domain/user and correlation ids (`corr-1`, `corr-q`).
> 
> **Secret canaries:** Read privacy tests replace fixed `const` exception secrets with per-run `Guid` values. Catalog invocation theories use an `includeToken` flag and generate fresh nonfunctional tokens at runtime instead of inline literals like `"extra"` or `"human.token"`, so strict reusable-secret controls pass without changing what behavior is exercised.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 7b890438e50df663a2762ccc44c0bdd0a8214d7b. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
